AdminGroupEnrollmentData.title: AdminGroupEnrollmentData
AdminGroupEnrollmentData.description: Request body for group enrollment actions.

AdminGroupEnrollmentResponse.title: AdminGroupEnrollmentResponse
AdminGroupEnrollmentResponse.description:
Response for ``POST /admin/item/group/enrollment``: the new enrollment
code (reset) or ``True`` (disable).

AdminGroupFullDataResponse.title: AdminGroupFullDataResponse
AdminGroupFullDataResponse.description:
Response for ``GET /admin/item/group/{group_id}``.

``GroupsProcessed.group_get_full_data`` returns the row merged with
``linked_groups_data``. Inherits ``AdminGroup`` and adds the two
enrichment fields.

AdminGroupListItem.title: AdminGroupListItem
AdminGroupListItem.description:
Row shape for ``GET /admin/items/groups``.

``GroupsProcessed.admin_get_groups`` returns the full ``groups`` row
merged with ``linked_groups_data`` (a denormalised array of
``{id, name}`` pairs from the linked groups). Inherits ``AdminGroup``
so the canonical group fields stay strict and only the two extra
columns are added on top.

AdminGroupNavItem.title: AdminGroupNavItem
AdminGroupNavItem.description:
Row shape for ``GET /admin/items/users/{nav}/groups``.

``UsersProcessed.admin_list_groups`` returns the full groups row with
extra merges: ``management`` adds ``linked_groups_data``
(with ``category_name``) and ``parent_category_name``;
``quotas_limits`` adds ``media_size`` / ``domains_size``. Fields kept
optional + the ``without`` strip on ``quotas_limits`` is reflected by
making ``enrollment``/``external_*``/``linked_groups`` optional here.

AdminGroupUpdateData.title: AdminGroupUpdateData
AdminGroupUpdateData.description: Request body for updating a group.

AdminGroupUserItem.title: AdminGroupUserItem
AdminGroupUserItem.description:
Row shape for ``GET /admin/items/group/{group_id}/users``.

``GroupsProcessed.get_users_in_group`` plucks ``id``, ``name``,
``username`` and ``photo`` only.

AdminHypervisorCreateData.title: AdminHypervisorCreateData
AdminHypervisorCreateData.description: Request body for creating/registering a hypervisor.

AdminHypervisorDisksFoundData.title: AdminHypervisorDisksFoundData
AdminHypervisorDisksFoundData.description: Request body for reporting disks found on hypervisor.

AdminHypervisorEnableData.title: AdminHypervisorEnableData
AdminHypervisorEnableData.description: Request body for enabling/disabling a hypervisor.

AdminHypervisorMediaDeleteData.title: AdminHypervisorMediaDeleteData
AdminHypervisorMediaDeleteData.description: Request body for deleting media paths.

AdminHypervisorMediaFoundData.title: AdminHypervisorMediaFoundData
AdminHypervisorMediaFoundData.description: Request body for reporting media found on hypervisor.

AdminHypervisorStatusResponse.title: AdminHypervisorStatusResponse
AdminHypervisorStatusResponse.description:
Response for ``GET /admin/item/hypervisor/status/{hyper_id}`` —
the trimmed status row (id, status, only_forced).

enable_virt_pool.description: Enable or disable the virt pool

AdminHypervisorVirtPoolUpdateData.title: AdminHypervisorVirtPoolUpdateData
AdminHypervisorVirtPoolUpdateData.description: Request body for updating hypervisor virt pool assignment.

AdminHypervisorWgAddrData.title: AdminHypervisorWgAddrData
AdminHypervisorWgAddrData.description: Request body for updating wireguard address.

AdminHypervisorWgAddrResponse.title: AdminHypervisorWgAddrResponse
AdminHypervisorWgAddrResponse.description:
Response for ``GET /admin/item/hypervisor/vm/wg_addr`` — the wireguard
table lookup result for the hypervisor host.

AdminLinkedGroupNamed.title: AdminLinkedGroupNamed
AdminLinkedGroupNamed.description:
``{id, name, category_name}`` lookup row used by the management nav
response for the ``linked_groups_data`` array.

AdminListDomainsData.title: AdminListDomainsData
AdminListDomainsData.description: Request body for listing domains (desktops or templates).

AdminLoginConfigResponse.title: AdminLoginConfigResponse
AdminLoginConfigResponse.description:
Raw response for the admin login-config read endpoints.

Returned by ``GET /admin/item/login-config`` (global) and
``GET /admin/item/login-config/{category_id}`` (per-category — the
service falls back to the global config when the category has no
overrides). Permissive shape because the underlying
``Configuration.login`` blob is admin-edited freeform; the public
``LoginConfigResponse`` (in ``api.schemas.login``) typed each field
individually for the consumer side, but the admin edit modal needs
the unmerged raw payload.

AdminMediaItem.title: AdminMediaItem
AdminMediaItem.description:
One row of ``GET /admin/items/media`` and ``GET /admin/items/media/{status}``.

The service returns the raw media doc merged with display-friendly
joined fields (category_name, group_name, user_name, domains
count). Permissive (``ConfigDict(extra="allow")``) because legacy
rows may carry fields the merger doesn't know about — losing them
silently was the apiv3 behaviour and the webapp admin tolerates it.

AdminMediaStatusCount.title: AdminMediaStatusCount
AdminMediaStatusCount.description:
One row of ``GET /media/status``.

The service emits ``{status, count}`` pairs from
``MediaProcessed.admin_get_media_status_count``. Status values are
DB-driven (``MediaStatusEnum`` plus historical strings), so the
field stays loose ``str``.

AdminMigrationErrorsResponse.title: AdminMigrationErrorsResponse
AdminMigrationErrorsResponse.description:
Response for ``GET /admin/item/user/migrate/check/{user_id}/{target_user_id}``.

Service returns the raw error list; the route wraps it as
``{"errors": [...]}``.

AdminMigrationStartedResponse.title: AdminMigrationStartedResponse
AdminMigrationStartedResponse.description:
Response for ``PUT /admin/item/user/migrate/{user_id}/{target_user_id}``.

On success the service returns ``({}, 200)``; on validation failure it
returns ``({"errors": [...]}, 428)``. Both shapes serialise through a
single optional-``errors`` model.

AdminMultipleActionsData.title: AdminMultipleActionsData
AdminMultipleActionsData.description: Request body for performing actions on multiple domains.

AdminPasswordPolicyResponse.title: AdminPasswordPolicyResponse
AdminPasswordPolicyResponse.description:
Response for ``GET /admin/item/user/password-policy/{user_id}``.

``UserPolicies.get_user_policy(subtype="password", ...)`` returns the
policy dict (or ``False`` when no policy applies). The route only ever
calls it with ``subtype="password"``, so the shape is the password
policy. ``False`` is normalised to ``{}`` by the route's
``isinstance(result, dict)`` guard so we don't have to model the
bool variant.

AdminPasswordResetData.title: AdminPasswordResetData
AdminPasswordResetData.description: Request body for resetting a user's password.

AdminQuotaCategoryLimits.title: AdminQuotaCategoryLimits
AdminQuotaCategoryLimits.description:
Category- (or group-) scoped limits block returned by
``QuotasProcess.process_category_limits`` /
``get_manager_usage`` / ``get_admin_usage``.

The two ``process_*_limits`` paths emit the full ``q``/``qp`` set;
the manager/admin-usage paths return only the counters
(``d``/``r``/``t``/``i``/``v``/``m``/``u``/``deployments``). All
``q``/``qp`` fields kept optional so the lighter shapes don't 500
here.

quota.description: Quota dict (desktops, templates, vcpus, memory, ...) or ``False`` if no quota is configured.

limits.description: Limits dict (the maximum the entity may set its own quota to) or ``False`` if no limits apply.

grouplimits.description: Group-level limits, only present on group quota lookups.

AdminQuotaResponse.title: AdminQuotaResponse
AdminQuotaResponse.description:
Configured quota / limits for a user, category or group.

The shape varies by ``kind``: user lookups return ``quota`` +
``limits``; category lookups return ``quota`` + ``limits``; group
lookups additionally include ``grouplimits``. ``Quotas.Get*Quota``
in the common helper is the source of truth.

AdminQuotaUserUsage.title: AdminQuotaUserUsage
AdminQuotaUserUsage.description:
Per-user quota usage block from ``QuotasProcess.process_user_quota``.

All ``q``/``qp`` fields are emitted unconditionally — when the user
has no quota set the service writes ``9999`` / ``0`` placeholders,
so the int variant covers both cases.

AdminQuotasResponse.title: AdminQuotasResponse
AdminQuotasResponse.description:
Response for ``GET /admin/items/quotas``.

``QuotasProcess.get`` always returns a ``user`` block and adds either
``limits`` (managers) or ``global`` (admins).

AdminRegisterVlansRequest.title: AdminRegisterVlansRequest
AdminRegisterVlansRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /admin/items/vlans``.

Sent by ``docker/hypervisor/src/vlans/vlans-db.py``: the hypervisor
reports the set of VLAN identifiers it has discovered so the API
can upsert the corresponding ``interfaces`` entries.

AdminRoleItem.title: AdminRoleItem
AdminRoleItem.description:
Row shape for ``GET /admin/items/roles``.

``UsersProcessed.get_roles`` plucks ``id``, ``name``,
``description`` (and orders by ``sortorder``).

AdminRoleUpdateData.title: AdminRoleUpdateData
AdminRoleUpdateData.description:
Request body for updating a role.

The route forces ``id`` from the URL path, so any ``id`` on the
body is ignored — declared optional so callers that include it for
symmetry don't 4xx, and the service receives the URL-derived id.

AdminSecondaryGroupRef.title: AdminSecondaryGroupRef
AdminSecondaryGroupRef.description:
Lightweight ``{id, name}`` group reference used by the user-full-data
response. Same pluck as ``GroupsProcessed.get_secondary_groups_data``.

AdminSecondaryGroupsData.title: AdminSecondaryGroupsData
AdminSecondaryGroupsData.description: Request body for secondary group operations.

AdminSecretCreateData.title: AdminSecretCreateData
AdminSecretCreateData.description: Request body for creating a secret.

AdminSecretCreateResponse.title: AdminSecretCreateResponse
AdminSecretCreateResponse.description:
Response for ``POST /admin/item/secret``.

Service returns ``{secret: <raw>}`` only — the JWT-signing key is
surfaced once and never read back.

AdminSecretItem.title: AdminSecretItem
AdminSecretItem.description:
Row shape for ``GET /admin/items/secrets``.

Backed by ``ApiAdmin.admin_table_list("secrets")`` — the secrets
table carries the same fields the create-endpoint advertises
(``id``/``kid``, ``category_id``, ``secret``, ``description``,
``role_id``).

AdminStorageDomain.title: AdminStorageDomain
AdminStorageDomain.description:
One row of ``GET /admin/items/storage/domains/{id}`` and
``GET /admin/items/media/domains/{id}``: the domain id + display name
the webapp admin lists. Permissive — joined fields differ.

categories.description: Category IDs to filter by (admin only)

AdminStorageFilterRequest.title: AdminStorageFilterRequest
AdminStorageFilterRequest.description: Request body for filtering admin storage listings.

AdminStorageInfo.title: AdminStorageInfo
AdminStorageInfo.description:
Response shape for ``GET /admin/item/storage/info/{id}`` and
``GET /admin/item/storage/search-info/{id}``.

Backed by ``AdminStorageService.get_storage_info`` /
``get_storage_search_info`` — qemu-img blob plus owner joins.
Permissive because those service methods merge sub-objects whose
keys differ per backend.

AdminStorageItem.title: AdminStorageItem
AdminStorageItem.description:
One row of ``GET /admin/items/storage`` and the by-status / by-role
variants. Permissive (``ConfigDict(extra="allow")``) because the
storage doc carries varied per-status fields the webapp admin
renders verbatim.

enqueued.description: Number of qemu-img-info refresh tasks enqueued.

AdminStorageRefreshResponse.title: AdminStorageRefreshResponse
AdminStorageRefreshResponse.description: Result of the running-desktops qemu-img-info refresh sweep.

AdminUserCreateData.title: AdminUserCreateData
AdminUserCreateData.description: Request body for creating a user.

AdminUserDesktopItem.title: AdminUserDesktopItem
AdminUserDesktopItem.description:
Row shape for ``GET /admin/items/user/{user_id}/desktops``.

``DomainsProcessed.list_by_kind_user("desktop", ...)`` plucks the
listed fields. ``status`` may be missing on freshly-created
desktops.

AdminUserFullDataResponse.title: AdminUserFullDataResponse
AdminUserFullDataResponse.description:
Response for ``GET /admin/item/user/{user_id}`` and ``/raw``.

``UsersProcessed.get_user_full_data`` enriches the cached user row with
``category_name``, ``group_name`` and ``secondary_groups_data``. Inherits
every ``AdminUser`` field (so half-deleted rows still serialize) and
surfaces the two name lookups + the secondary-group expansion. The raw
variant goes through ``Caches.get_cached_user_with_names`` which already
merges the same name fields, so a single model covers both.

AdminUserIdResponse.title: AdminUserIdResponse
AdminUserIdResponse.description:
Response for ``GET /admin/item/user/email-category/{email}/{category}``.

Returns ``{id: <user-id-or-None>}`` — service may return ``None`` when
no user matches.

AdminUserImpersonateJwtResponse.title: AdminUserImpersonateJwtResponse
AdminUserImpersonateJwtResponse.description: Response for ``GET /admin/item/jwt/{user_id}`` — a single signed JWT.

AdminUserNavItem.title: AdminUserNavItem
AdminUserNavItem.description:
Row shape for ``GET /admin/items/users/{nav}/users``.

``UsersProcessed.admin_list_users`` plucks the ``AdminUser`` fields and,
depending on ``nav``, merges either the ``*_name`` lookups
(``management``) or quota usage counters (``quotas_limits``). Both nav
branches share the base id/name columns; the divergent fields are kept
optional so a single model covers both shapes.

AdminUserSchemaResponse.title: AdminUserSchemaResponse
AdminUserSchemaResponse.description: Response for user schema (roles, categories, groups).

AdminUserSearchItem.title: AdminUserSearchItem
AdminUserSearchItem.description:
Row shape for ``POST /admin/items/users/search``.

``Alloweds.get_table_term`` plucks ``id``/``name``/``uid`` for admins
and adds ``category`` for managers. Both fields kept optional so a
single model handles either pluck variant.

AdminUserUpdateData.title: AdminUserUpdateData
AdminUserUpdateData.description: Request body for updating one or more users.

AdminUserVpnFileResponse.title: AdminUserVpnFileResponse
AdminUserVpnFileResponse.description:
Response for the two VPN config/install endpoints.

``IsardVpn.vpn_data`` returns ``{kind: "file", name, ext, mime,
content}`` for both ``config`` (wireguard ``.conf``) and ``install``
(a ``sh``/``vb`` setup script).

AdminVirtInstallSaveResponse.title: AdminVirtInstallSaveResponse
AdminVirtInstallSaveResponse.description:
Response of ``POST /admin/item/domains/xml_sections/{domain_id}/save_virt_install``.

Only ``id`` and ``name`` are returned to the route layer (see the
route's ``record["id"], record["name"]`` slice).

AdminVirtInstallXmlSectionsSaveResponse.title: AdminVirtInstallXmlSectionsSaveResponse
AdminVirtInstallXmlSectionsSaveResponse.description:
Response of ``POST /admin/virt_install/xml_sections/{virt_id}``.

Mirrors ``save_virt_install_xml_sections`` which returns
``{xml: <merged>, valid: True}``.

AdminVpnConnectionsDisconnectRequest.title: AdminVpnConnectionsDisconnectRequest
AdminVpnConnectionsDisconnectRequest.description:
Top-level JSON array body for ``DELETE /admin/vpn_connections``.

Aligned with the FastAPI operation id ``vpn_connections_disconnect``.

categories.description: List of allowed categories. If False, no categories are allowed.

roles.description: List of allowed roles. If False, no roles are allowed.

users.description: List of allowed users. If False, no users are allowed.

AllowedGetRequest.title: AllowedGetRequest
AllowedGetRequest.description: Request body for getting allowed access list for a table item.

selected.description: List of currently selected allowed users and groups

available_groups.description: List of groups that the user is allowed to access and share items with

indeterminate_groups.description: List of groups that have some, but not all, users allowed

AllowedTableEntityItem.title: AllowedTableEntityItem
AllowedTableEntityItem.description:
Enriched roles/categories row from ``Alloweds.get_allowed`` —
pluck'd to ``id, name, uid, parent_category``.

AllowedTableGroupItem.title: AllowedTableGroupItem
AllowedTableGroupItem.description:
Enriched group row from ``Alloweds.get_allowed`` — pluck'd to
``id, name, uid, parent_category`` and merged with ``category_name``.

AllowedTableResponse.title: AllowedTableResponse
AllowedTableResponse.description:
Response model for ``POST /allowed/table/{table}``.

Mirrors the dict returned by ``Alloweds.get_allowed`` — each
bucket is either ``False`` (allow-none) or a list of enriched
rows. Buckets are individually optional because the underlying
``allowed`` dict may not declare every key on legacy rows.

AllowedTableUserItem.title: AllowedTableUserItem
AllowedTableUserItem.description:
Enriched user row from ``Alloweds.get_allowed`` — pluck'd to
``id, name, uid, username, photo`` and merged with
``category_name``/``group_name``.

AllowedTermItem.title: AllowedTermItem
AllowedTermItem.description:
Single autocomplete row returned by
``POST /admin/allowed/term/{table}``.

The service overrides the pluck per-table:
``users`` adds ``uid, role, username, category_name, group_name``;
``groups`` adds ``parent_category, category_name``. The webapp's
select2 templates render those fields (e.g.
``static/js/snippets/alloweds.js`` shows
``item.name [item.uid] (item.category_name)``), so the model must
let them pass through — ``extra='allow'`` preserves them; without
it Pydantic strips every field except ``id``/``name`` and the
select2 labels become ``undefined``.

exclude_role.description: Role to exclude from user results

AllowedTermRequest.title: AllowedTermRequest
AllowedTermRequest.description: Request body for searching table items by term.

groups.description: List of allowed groups. If None, the field is not updated.

users.description: List of allowed users. If None, the field is not updated.

allowed.description: Allowed access configuration with roles, categories, groups, users

AllowedUpdateRequest.title: AllowedUpdateRequest
AllowedUpdateRequest.description: Request body for updating allowed access on a table item.

categories.description: List of category IDs to filter

AnalyticsCategoriesRequest.title: AnalyticsCategoriesRequest
AnalyticsCategoriesRequest.description: Request body for analytics endpoints that filter by categories.

AnalyticsGraphConfigResponse.title: AnalyticsGraphConfigResponse
AnalyticsGraphConfigResponse.description:
Row in the ``analytics`` table — see ``AnalyticsGraphCreateRequest``
for the writeable fields. ``id`` is auto-assigned by RethinkDB and
``grouping_name`` is resolved by the list endpoint.

Every field is optional: rows written before the create/update schemas
carried these fields persisted without them.

AnalyticsGraphCreateRequest.title: AnalyticsGraphCreateRequest
AnalyticsGraphCreateRequest.description:
Request body for creating an analytics graph configuration.

``id`` is absent on purpose: the admin form strips it and RethinkDB
assigns the primary key.

AnalyticsGraphUpdateRequest.title: AnalyticsGraphUpdateRequest
AnalyticsGraphUpdateRequest.description:
Request body for updating an analytics graph configuration.

``id`` is absent on purpose: the edit form posts it in the body and
it must not reach the update.

categories.description: List of category IDs to filter

months_without_use.description: Number of months without use to consider for removal

AnalyticsSuggestedRemovalsRequest.title: AnalyticsSuggestedRemovalsRequest
AnalyticsSuggestedRemovalsRequest.description: Request body for suggested removals endpoint.

AutoDeleteEnabledRequest.title: AutoDeleteEnabledRequest
AutoDeleteEnabledRequest.description: Request to set auto delete enabled

start.description: The start time of the availability period.

end.description: The end time of the availability period.

BacklogRollupRow.title: BacklogRollupRow
BacklogRollupRow.description:
One ``(pool, category, tier)`` backlog rollup row — the ``GET
/admin/items/queues/backlog`` payload is a bare list of these (P2.4 §2.4).

BackupConfigResponse.title: BackupConfigResponse
BackupConfigResponse.description:
Response shape for ``GET /admin/item/backups/config``.

Mirrors the dict returned by ``AdminBackupsService.get_backup_config``.

BackupConfigSchedule.title: BackupConfigSchedule
BackupConfigSchedule.description: Schedule hours per backup scope (``None`` = unscheduled).

BackupIntegrityResponse.title: BackupIntegrityResponse
BackupIntegrityResponse.description: Response shape for ``GET /admin/item/backups/integrity`` and the matching PUT.

integrity_enabled.description: Enable or disable the weekly run

BackupIntegritySetRequest.title: BackupIntegritySetRequest
BackupIntegritySetRequest.description: Request body for the weekly borg integrity check toggle.

BackupItem.title: BackupItem
BackupItem.description:
One row of ``GET /admin/items/backups``.

Permissive (``ConfigDict(extra="allow")``) because legacy backup
rows carry assorted free-form metadata in ``details`` that the
webapp admin renders verbatim. The required fields are the ones
the route depends on for sorting / display.

details.description: Backup details with checks, warnings, time_breakdown

BackupReportRequest.title: BackupReportRequest
BackupReportRequest.description:
Request body for backup report submission.

Permissive (``ConfigDict(extra="allow")``) to mirror ``BackupItem``: the
backupninja parser sends rich, free-form report fields on top of the ones
declared below (``disk_types``, ``actions``, the ``*_actions`` counts,
``duration``, ``summary``, ``backup_types_status``, ``filesystem_metrics``,
...). The webapp backups view renders several of these verbatim
(``total_actions``/``successful_actions``/``warning_actions``/
``failed_actions``, ``duration``, ``backup_types_status``). Without
``extra="allow"`` pydantic silently dropped every one of them, leaving the
stored record — and the admin view — with only status/type/scope/timestamp.

exists.description: Whether a bastion target exists for this desktop.

bastion_ssh_port.description: The global bastion SSH port (None if disabled).

BastionActiveResponse.title: BastionActiveResponse
BastionActiveResponse.description:
Lightweight, read-only bastion status for a desktop.

Returned by the non-mutating ``/bastion/active`` endpoint used by the
desktop-card "Bastion" entry: it never creates a target and carries just
enough to decide whether to open the read-only access modal (``ssh.enabled``
/ ``http.enabled``) and to render the access links.

BastionActiveSshStatus.title: BastionActiveSshStatus
BastionActiveSshStatus.description: SSH access status without exposing the authorized keys.

authorized_keys.description: List of SSH public keys to authorize for bastion SSH access.

BastionAuthorizedKeysRequest.title: BastionAuthorizedKeysRequest
BastionAuthorizedKeysRequest.description: Request model for updating bastion SSH authorized keys

authorized_keys.description: List of SSH public keys to be authorized for the bastion SSH access. If empty, the authorized keys will be cleared.

enabled.description: Whether there is any bastion access to show. False when bastion is globally disabled, the desktop has no target, or neither SSH nor HTTP access is enabled on it.

custom_domains.description: Custom domains configured for the target. The access URLs above are only built from the first one.

ssh_enabled.description: Whether bastion SSH access is enabled.

ssh_command.description: Ready-to-run SSH command, if SSH access is enabled.

http_enabled.description: Whether bastion HTTP access is enabled.

http_url.description: Public HTTP URL, if HTTP access is enabled.

https_url.description: Public HTTPS URL, if HTTP access is enabled.

BastionDirectViewerResponse.title: BastionDirectViewerResponse
BastionDirectViewerResponse.description:
Read-only bastion connection info for the direct viewer.

Reachable by anyone holding the share link, so it carries only what is
needed to connect — target id, domains and ready-to-use URLs — and no key
material nor owner data. The URLs are built server-side because the direct
viewer cannot read the config (``bastion_domain``, ports) they need.

domain_name.description: The domain name to be set for the bastion target of the desktop.

domain_verification_required.description: Whether domain verification is required for bastion domains.

BastionDomainVerificationConfigResponse.title: BastionDomainVerificationConfigResponse
BastionDomainVerificationConfigResponse.description: Response model for bastion domain verification configuration

domains.description: List of custom domain names for the bastion target. Maximum 10.

BastionDomainsRequest.title: BastionDomainsRequest
BastionDomainsRequest.description: Request model for updating bastion custom domains

domains.description: Up to 10 bastion domain names to set for the desktop. An empty list clears the domains.

BastionDomainsUpdateRequest.title: BastionDomainsUpdateRequest
BastionDomainsUpdateRequest.description: Bulk update of the bastion ``domains`` list (up to 10).

proxy_protocol.description: If true, the bastion sends a PROXY protocol v2 header to the guest, preserving the real client IP.

BookableItemResponse.title: BookableItemResponse
BookableItemResponse.description:
A bookable vGPU reservable for the admin Bookables list.

``categories`` are the distinct names of the categories that delegated GPU
cards backing this reservable belong to (empty when only global/undelegated
cards back it). The webapp renders them as green delegated-category tags.

vgpus.description: List of vGPU profile IDs associated with the booking event

BookingEventReservables.title: BookingEventReservables
BookingEventReservables.description: Reservables associated with a booking event

BookingPlanResponse.title: BookingPlanResponse
BookingPlanResponse.description: Response model for a booking plan

BookingPriorityDesktopResponse.title: BookingPriorityDesktopResponse
BookingPriorityDesktopResponse.description:
Response model for booking priority desktop.

The dict returned by ``Bookings.get_user_priority(...)`` (per-vgpu
priorities + the most-restrictive ``forbid_time/max_time/max_items``)
merged with the desktop ``name``. ``max_time`` and ``max_items`` may
be ``None`` when no priority rule matched.

BrandingLogo.title: BrandingLogo
BrandingLogo.description: Branding logo configuration. data is a base64 data URL.

BrandingResponse.title: BrandingResponse
BrandingResponse.description:
Response shape for ``GET /admin/item/category/{id}/branding``.

Mirrors the request shape — ``BrandingUpdateData`` — but is a
distinct class because the response side of branding is the
persisted value (i.e. ``Category.branding``), and the response
model is what FastAPI uses to filter the wire payload. Keeps both
sub-objects optional because freshly-created categories may have
no branding row at all.

BrandingUpdateData.title: BrandingUpdateData
BrandingUpdateData.description: Request body for updating category branding.

template_id.description: ID of the template to clone from.

name.description: Base name for the created desktops.

allowed.description: Set of users / groups / categories / roles to fan out to. Each member receives one desktop.

BulkCreatePersistentDesktopsRequest.title: BulkCreatePersistentDesktopsRequest
BulkCreatePersistentDesktopsRequest.description:
Request body for ``POST /items/desktops/bulk-create``.

Creates many persistent desktops from a single template for a set
of users / groups / categories / roles. The actual fan-out happens
inside ``CommonDesktops.bulk_create_desktops``.

exceptions.description: List of error messages for deployments that could not be deleted

ids.description: List of deployment IDs to delete

permanent.description: Whether to permanently delete the deployments

ids.description: List of desktop IDs to update.

BulkEditDesktopsRequest.title: BulkEditDesktopsRequest
BulkEditDesktopsRequest.description:
Request body for ``PUT /items/desktops/bulk-edit``.

The route applies a partial update to every desktop in ``ids``; the
remaining fields are forwarded to ``CommonDesktops.update_desktop``
in bulk mode.

CardResponse.title: CardResponse
CardResponse.description:
Single card response.

Permissive (``ConfigDict(extra="allow")``) because card payloads

UsageRetentionConfig.title: UsageRetentionConfig
UsageRetentionConfig.description:
Tiered retention policy for ``usage_consumption``.

Daily rows are kept untouched for ``daily_months`` months. Rows
aged between ``daily_months`` and ``weekly_months`` collapse into
weekly buckets (Monday-of-week, summed ``inc``, last ``abs`` of
the bucket). Older rows collapse into monthly buckets (first-of-
month, same aggregation). When ``total_months`` is set, anything
older is deleted; when unset, monthly history is retained
indefinitely.

Per-field bounds are enforced by Pydantic. The cross-field
invariants ``weekly_months > daily_months`` and (when set)
``total_months >= weekly_months`` are enforced at the route /
service boundary via :meth:`assert_tier_ordering`. They are NOT
a ``model_validator`` because raising a ``ValueError`` from one
propagates a ``RequestValidationError`` whose ``ctx['error']``
holds the raw ``ValueError``, and the project's global handler
serialises ``exc.errors()`` to JSON — non-serialisable types in
``ctx`` would crash the handler with a 500.

password.description: Password for accessing the desktop using RDP.

file_rdpgw.description: Configuration for file-based RDP gateway access.

file_rdpvpn.description: Configuration for file-based RDP VPN access.

vgpus.description: List of IDs of vGPUs that can be reserved for the desktop. If None, no vGPUs can be reserved nor used. Each ID must be a valid vGPU ID.
